messages.subject: Options List on Wiki
parts:
I thought maybe this should be separated from the other thread. 
A list of options for fine tuning your plots can be found at the following address. It is very much a work in progress.

http://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/+opts()-List

Brian, 

Thanks for dissecting the code a bit, I'll add them when I get the time. I started to add some basic examples and I'll try and add pictures showing what's going on as well. 

Is there also a way to tell if there are more/hidden attributes of theme_text/segment/line/rect(). I've tried to list what I've found on the intertubes and in Hadley's book, but I'm sure it's not comprehensive. 

And if it's confusing as to what I'm referring to, please see the following:

theme_text()
color
size
angle
hjust
vjust
face = bold ital

MORE????

Brandon

On Wed, Sep 22, 2010 at 21:57, Brian Diggs <dig...@ohsu.edu> wrote:
>
> I thought I'd browse the source code to see if there were any more,
> and it seems that theme_gray() is the canonical reference (theme_set
> in theme.r gets its list of valid names from theme_gray()).
> names(theme_gray()) gives the list of possible options.  However, I
> took it a step further to pull out what types of things they can
> take.  The following code summarizes them:
>
> tg <- theme_gray()
> op <- data.frame(opt = names(tg), class = laply(tg, class))
> op[op$class=="theme","type"] <- laply(tg[op$class=="theme"], attr,
> "type")
> op
> #                  opt     class    type
> # 1          axis.line     theme     any
> # 2        axis.text.x     theme    text
> # 3        axis.text.y     theme    text
> # 4         axis.ticks     theme segment
> # 5       axis.title.x     theme    text
> # 6       axis.title.y     theme    text
> # 7  axis.ticks.length      unit    <NA>
> # 8  axis.ticks.margin      unit    <NA>
> # 9  legend.background     theme     box
> # 10        legend.key     theme     box
> # 11   legend.key.size      unit    <NA>
> # 12       legend.text     theme    text
> # 13      legend.title     theme    text
> # 14   legend.position character    <NA>
> # 15  panel.background     theme     box
> # 16      panel.border     theme     any
> # 17  panel.grid.major     theme    line
> # 18  panel.grid.minor     theme    line
> # 19      panel.margin      unit    <NA>
> # 20  strip.background     theme     box
> # 21      strip.text.x     theme    text
> # 22      strip.text.y     theme    text
> # 23   plot.background     theme     box
> # 24        plot.title     theme    text
> # 25       plot.margin      unit    <NA>
>
> For the type (which is only defined for the themes), "box" is set with
> theme_rect; "any" is a theme_blank() in theme_gray(), so you can fall
> back to the printed documentation for what theme type it should be.
>
> In particular, the additional ones not already listed on the wiki are:
>
> axis.ticks.length (unit)
> axis.ticks.margin (unit)
> legend.key.size (unit)
> panel.margin (unit)
> plot.margin (unit)
>
> As to further description of some of the options:
>
> legend.position is either a numeric vector of length two or a
> character value in "top", "bottom", "left", "right", or "none".  If it
> is a numeric vector of length 2, they are the x and y coordinates of
> the legend (not sure in what units/scale) and and additional option,
> legend.justification, is used as the justification of the viewport
> (just arugment of viewport()). [Derived from reading plot-render.r]
>
>

> > >>>> >> data2 <- data.frame(Corpus = factor(rep(1:2, 3)),

> > >>>> >> q <- ggplot(data2, aes(x = x, y = f1, fill = Corpus))

> > >>>> >>     scale_fill_manual('Corpus', value = c('1' = '#00a37c', '2' =
> > >>>> '#2dab00'))
> > >>>> >> +
> > >>>> >>     coord_flip() + opts(legend.position = c(0.9, 0.15))
